content: This document does not include all potential drug interactions. It is essential to maintain a comprehensive list of all products you use, including prescription medications, over-the-counter drugs, and herbal supplements, and share this information with your healthcare provider and pharmacist. Certain medications can influence the elimination of efavirenz from your body, potentially altering its effectiveness. Conversely, efavirenz can accelerate the removal of many other drugs from your system, which may impact their efficacy. Some antiretroviral drugs used to treat HIV, such as elvitegravir or other NNRTIs (e.g., etravirine, nevirapine, rilpivirine), may interact with efavirenz. If you are taking atazanavir alongside efavirenz, you may also need to take ritonavir to ensure proper therapeutic effects. Additionally, efavirenz may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives, such as pills, patches, or rings, which could result in unintended pregnancy. Discuss with your healthcare provider whether you should use a reliable backup method of contraception while on this medication. Carefully review the labels of all your medications, including those for allergies or cough and cold, as they may contain ingredients that cause drowsiness. Efavirenz may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as urine cannabinoid tests, potentially leading to false results. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center without delay. U.S. residents can reach the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. Before starting efavirenz and during its use, laboratory and medical tests should be conducted. These may include liver function tests, viral load assessments, T-cell counts, and measurements of cholesterol and triglyceride levels. It is crucial to attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose of efavirenz, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last revised in September 2024. It is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
